title: Reading Drill — Drawing Patterns on Fabric
description: One short passage, five questions. Recommended time: 8 minutes.

passages.title: Drawing Patterns on Fabric
passages.body:
**A** A craft tutor asked learners to draw a repeated design by hand. Small errors close to the first edge became much larger as the pattern crossed the fabric.

**B** The class drew a light guide grid before attempting a second version. Most students chose a fixed starting corner rather than trying to align the pattern by eye.

**C** Both versions were displayed in the corridor. Captions asked visitors to look for the first misalignment instead of simply deciding which fabric they liked best.

questions.prompt: Small errors close to the first ______ became much larger as the pattern crossed the fabric.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: Small errors close to the first edge became much larger as the pattern crossed the fabric.

questions.prompt: Most students chose a fixed starting corner rather than trying to align the pattern by ______.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: Most students chose a fixed starting corner rather than trying to align the pattern by eye.

questions.prompt: Captions asked visitors to look for the first ______ instead of simply deciding which fabric they liked best.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: Captions asked visitors to look for the first misalignment instead of simply deciding which fabric they liked best.

questions.prompt: The second version used a visible guide while it was being drawn.
questions.instructions: Does this statement agree with the information in the passage?
questions.explanation: The class drew a light guide grid before attempting a second version. Most students chose a fixed starting corner rather than trying to align the pattern by eye.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph mentions what viewers were asked to locate in the display?
questions.explanation: Both versions were displayed in the corridor. Captions asked visitors to look for the first misalignment instead of simply deciding which fabric they liked best.
